topics.title: What Do Different Food Items Contain?
objectives: Student can test for the presence of starch in a food sample using iodine solution
Student can demonstrate the presence of proteins in a food item using copper sulphate and caustic soda solutions
Student can identify the presence of fats in food by using a paper rub test
visualIdeas: a illustration of a dropper adding iodine to a potato slice with a blue-black color change
a test tube changing to violet color when solutions are added to test for proteins

topics.title: What Do Various Nutrients Do for Our Body?
objectives: Student can match major food sources with their corresponding primary nutrients like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
Student can list the biological roles of vitamins and minerals in maintaining body health
Student can explain the importance of dietary fibres and water in human digestion
visualIdeas: a colorful plate diagram categorizing food items into energy-giving, body-building, and protective foods
a simple diagram of the digestive tract showing roughage assisting in moving waste

topics.title: Balanced Diet
objectives: Student can define a balanced diet in terms of nutrient proportion and variety
Student can design a simple, cost-effective meal plan that constitutes a balanced diet
Student can state the loss of nutrients that occurs due to incorrect cooking and washing practices
visualIdeas: a pie chart of a meal plate showing the ideal proportions of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and vitamins
a comparison graphic of vegetables washed before cutting versus after cutting to show vitamin loss

topics.title: Deficiency Diseases
objectives: Student can correlate specific vitamin and mineral deficiencies with their corresponding diseases
Student can identify symptoms of diseases like scurvy, rickets, goitre, and anemia
visualIdeas: a summary table linking vitamins/minerals to deficiency diseases and their diagnostic symptoms
a line drawing of a neck showing thyroid swelling characteristic of goitre

topics.title: Objects Around Us
objectives: Student can list the different materials from which a single everyday object can be manufactured

a sorting bin graphic demonstrating grouping of glass, metal, plastics, and wood

topics.title: Properties of Materials
objectives: Student can distinguish between lustrous and non-lustrous materials by visual inspection

two beakers showing salt completely dissolving versus sand settling at the bottom

a conical pine tree showing how sloped branches shed snow easily

topics.title: Aquatic Habitats
